page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It includes a bundled local NVMe SSD storage capacity of 3780 GB, managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25%. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which contribute to top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is robust, achieving 205.9 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 132.81 GB/sec for write operations.

With its high-capacity local NVMe SSD and top-tier database operations benchmark results, this server is highly suitable for database hosting, Redis deployments, and static web serving. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in small-to-medium LLM inference tasks, though performance scales down to average levels for larger 70B models. The hardware profile offers high resource density and a balanced compute-to-memory ratio, providing qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise workloads that require high-speed local storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the Dadsv7 family, powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 3780 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers top-tier single-core performance and strong multi-core capabilities, supported by AVX-512 instruction sets. Benchmarks highlight exceptional database operations and single-threaded compression speeds, alongside strong memory bandwidth. Lacking a dedicated GPU, it is not intended for heavy graphics acceleration but excels in data-intensive workloads. The balanced resource allocation and high-speed local storage make it highly efficient for database hosting, Redis deployments, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference.
